_doc: Per-slug inputs for atlas/refresh.py (weekly Atlas refresh).
check_url: URL the reachability check uses instead of canonical_url, only where the canonical page does not answer 2xx by design (e.g. an API root).
numbers: simple numeric mappings from a public JSON endpoint (no HTML scraping, no money judgments). Each has a stable id.
value: either path (dot path to one number in the JSON) or agg over a list: {list, op: count|sum, field, where} with where values compared literally ('*' = present and non-empty).
match: an existing claim (by source_url + unit) this mapping continues. If that claim has a different basis, it is left untouched and a new claim is added.
A changed value is a re-observation: the claim gets the new value + observed_at (UTC), the previous value goes into claim.history. Past records are never rewritten.
basis: direct_observation = counted by us from the raw list; operator_claim = a total the operator's own stats endpoint reports (kept as operator_claim per atlas/PROTOCOL.md).
on_change_note: shown in the refresh PR for human follow-up.

statement: the claim text, regenerated from the same fetch on every refresh. {value} = the mapped number; {a.b.c} = another number from the same JSON (path mappings only; it must be in quote_fields so check.py can re-render the text from the claim's quote). A number that changes inside the text (a 7-day count beside a lifetime total) is a re-observation too. Without a statement, check.py fails when the old text holds numbers that are neither the value nor in the quote.
verify: optional {url, note} copied onto the claim: a smaller cross-check an agent can fetch within normal limits (same domain as url). Only real operator URLs; no invented totals.
agg.decimals: optional on a sum over atomic token units (e.g. 6 for USDC): the integer sum is divided once by 10^decimals, so the value is in whole tokens.

agg.fail_if_more: optional on a single-page read (no paginate): the name of the response's own completeness flag (e.g. has_more). If it is missing or not false, the read fails instead of publishing an undercount.

replications: optional {format, repo, workflow, branch}: replication counts for a register where review means replication (atlas/site/replications.py). The files are read at the newest commit on branch whose workflow push run succeeded and counted the way that validator counts; the record (counts, pinned commit, run URL) goes to atlas/data/replications.json and is published as `replications` on the card.
